In order to graduate, the university requires an overall core GPA of 2.0. Students must also complete, within the first 4 semesters as a music major: MU 1040 , MU 1121A , MU 1131A , MU 1201 , and MU 2211A , plus a minimum of 2 primary ensemble units. MU 1030 - World of Music (3) [GE 3A] MU 1040 - Careers in Music (3) MU 1080 - Introduction to Music Technology (3) MU 1121A - Class Piano I (1) MU 1131A - Class Piano II (1) MU 1201 - Introduction to Music Theory (3) MU 1811 - Performance Studio Lower Division (1) (4 units required) MU 2121A - Class Piano III (1) MU 2131A - Class Piano IV (1) MU 2202 - Music Theory: Classical I (3) MU 2211A - Musicianship I (1) MU 2221A - Musicianship II (1) MU 2700 - Performance Seminar (1) (4 units required) MU 3040 - Beginning Conducting (2) MU 3211A - Musicianship III (1) MU 3221A - Musicianship IV (1) MU 3940S - Music Studies Integration - Service Learning (1) MU 4180 - Western Classical Traditions I (3) MU 4190 - Western Classical Traditions II (3) MU 4610 - Senior Recital Studio (1) MU 4621 - Senior Recital (1) PHY 1050 - The Physics of Musical Sound (3) [GE 5A] PHY 1050L - Physics of Musical Sound Laboratory (1) [GE 5C] DAN 4490 - Dance in Contemporary Culture (3) [GE 4C] Additional Music Theory Courses: 6

courses.title: World of Music
courses.description: [GE 3A] Introduction to selected music cultures of the world. At least one music culture from each continent will be covered.

courses.title: Careers in Music
courses.description: Survey of careers in music and related fields, with emphasis on entrepreneurship and individual career options and planning. Overview of the roles and responsibilities in music performance, education, composition, production, and business.

courses.title: Introduction to Music Technology
courses.description: Introduction to the essential elements and application of computer-based music technology. Principles, uses, and techniques for working with MIDI, notation, and sequencing software and hardware.

courses.title: Class Piano I
courses.description: Beginning class piano instruction. Development of ability to play simple solo and duet compositions and chords in all keys. Chord progressions and harmonization of melodies using primary chords. Transposition. Technical studies and scales.

courses.title: Class Piano II
courses.description: Continuing class piano instruction. Simple solo and duet compositions and chords in all keys. Chord progressions and harmonization of melodies using primary and secondary chords. Transposition, modulation, simple improvisation. Technical studies and all major and minor scales.
courses.prerequisites: Music majors only; and MU 112A or MU 1121A or equivalent knowledge via instructor approval.

courses.title: Introduction to Music Theory
courses.description: Reading, playing, singing, listening to and analyzing: rhythms, simple and compound meters, dotted notes; the pitches of the clefs, major and minor scales and key signatures, altered minor scales, triads, triads in major and minor keys and their inversions, minor key signatures, major and minor key relationships. Corequisite(s): MU 2211A .
courses.prerequisites: Placement according to department entrance/placement exam.

courses.title: Performance Studio Lower Division
courses.description: Repertoire and technical studies as appropriate for each individual instrument or voice. Jury examination at the end of each semester. A series of 15 specialized individual instruction lessons for students enrolled in the Bachelor of Music only. Corequisite(s): MU 2700 and appropriate ensemble.
courses.prerequisites: Bachelor of Music major and permission to enroll by audition only.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Repeatable up to 6 units. Total credit limited by option.

courses.title: Class Piano III
courses.description: Second year of class piano instruction for music majors. Continued development of music reading and performance skills, covering compositions of many styles. Transposition, harmonization in various keyboard styles, improvisation, ensemble and accompaniment study. Technical studies and all major/ minor scales.
courses.prerequisites: Music majors only; and MU 113A, MU 1131A or equivalent.

courses.title: Class Piano IV
courses.description: Final semester of class piano instruction for music majors. Continued development of music reading and performance skills, covering compositions of many styles. Transposition, harmonization in various keyboard styles, improvisation, ensemble and accompaniment skills. Proficiency in all scales and arpeggios, sight-reading.
courses.prerequisites: Music majors only; and MU 212A, MU 2121A or equivalent.

courses.title: Music Theory: Classical I
courses.description: Materials and methods of composition and analysis for Western classical music, focusing mainly on diatonic materials. Scale realizations, cadences, related-key modulations, the Rule of the Octave, typical patterns (schemata), and four-part writing. Study of forms, including sentence, period, small binary, and small ternary (rounded binary). The student must be enrolled in musicianship concurrently with all theory classes unless they have completed all musicianship courses for their degree program.

courses.title: Musicianship I
courses.description: Drill and practice of sight-reading skills and rhythmic and melodic dictation, including software-assisted tutoring. Should be taken during the same semester as MU 1201. Corequisite(s): MU 1201 .
courses.prerequisites: Placement according to department entrance/placement exam.

courses.title: Musicianship II
courses.description: Drill and practice of sight-reading skills and rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic dictation including software-assisted tutoring.

courses.title: Performance Seminar
courses.description: Weekly seminar/workshop with opportunity to perform for other students and encourage discussion of technique, interpretation, and style. May be taken unlimited times. Corequisite(s): Concurrent enrollment in a studio course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: May be repeated up to 10 units.

courses.title: Beginning Conducting
courses.description: Introduction to the basic elements of conducting, including: non-verbal communication and gesture, hand independence, baton technique, preparatory beats, patterns, cues, releases, fermatas, score study and problem-solving rehearsal skills.
courses.prerequisites: MU 2211A , MU 1131A , and MU 2201 or MU 2202 .

courses.title: Musicianship III
courses.description: Drill and practice of sight-reading skills and rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic dictation including software-assisted tutoring.

courses.title: Musicianship IV
courses.description: Drill and practice of sight-reading skills and rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic dictation including software-assisted tutoring.

courses.title: Music Studies Integration - Service Learning
courses.description: Integration of the creative, performance, technological, educational, and business aspects of music. Semester-long group projects in conjunction with a community partner, resulting in a finished performance or production with a significant service-learning component. Service learning course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.

courses.title: Western Classical Traditions I
courses.description: Examination of the history of European and American classical music styles and their cultural influences prior to 1900. Research, listening.

courses.title: Western Classical Traditions II
courses.description: Examination of the history of European and American classical music styles and their cultural influences from 1900 to the present. Research, listening.

courses.title: Senior Recital Studio
courses.description: Weekly individual instructional lessons. Repertoire and technical studies in preparation for senior recital. Corequisite(s): MU 4621 and MU 2700 .

courses.title: Senior Recital
courses.description: Completion of a recital. Repertoire to be determined by, and work to be accomplished under the supervision of appropriate faculty member. Corequisite(s): MU 4610 and MU 2700 .

courses.title: The Physics of Musical Sound
courses.description: [GE 5A] The fundamentals of acoustics and its application to music-vibrations, wave, hearing, pure tones, complex tones, resonance, scales, consonance, and the physics of musical instruments. Corequisite(s): PHY 1050L .

courses.title: Physics of Musical Sound Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] Laboratory to accompany PHY 1050. Experimental study of sound, music, and related physical phenomena. Corequisite(s): PHY 1050 .

courses.title: Dance in Contemporary Culture
courses.description: [GE 4C] Dance in contemporary culture takes a look at the historical, cultural and social references that dance makes in society and contemporary culture. This includes multicultural and festival trends, community arts, experimental or non-traditional theatre, dance and body culture, dance and the body politic, dance, race, and the objectified gaze, gender perspectives, multi-media experience and traditions emerging from pop culture, technology and other contemporary sources found in dance.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Jazz and Pop Harmony and Techniques
courses.description: The study of the harmonic and rhythmic idioms used in popular music and jazz. Covers the aural and written language of chord symbols, analysis and practical use of typical pop and jazz chord progressions and harmonies, the writing of lead sheets, using a “rhythm section,” and an introduction to commercial and jazz arranging techniques. The student must be enrolled in musicianship concurrently with all theory classes unless they have completed all musicianship courses for their degree program.

courses.title: 20th and 21st Century Music Theory
courses.description: Survey of music theory approaches to Western music from the 20th century to the present. Study of representative works in various styles and genres, including a variety of relevant analytical and compositional techniques. The student must be enrolled in musicianship concurrently with all theory classes unless they have completed all musicianship courses for their degree program.

courses.title: Tonal Counterpoint
courses.description: Study and experience in analyzing and writing tonal counterpoint. Including modes, canon, species counterpoint, contrapuntal techniques. Vocal polyphony and instrumental inventions and fugues.

courses.title: Music Theory: Classical II
courses.description: Materials and methods of composition and analysis for Western music, focusing mainly on chromatic materials. Typical chromatic patterns (schemata) and enharmonic modulations. Transformation theory. Study of forms, including lied, and sonata forms. Applications to film, television, and video game music.

courses.title: Introduction to Music Education
courses.description: Exploration of music learning research and music education philosophies and methods in American music education. Discovery of current trends in contemporary inclusive music education. Includes 20 hours of field observation.

courses.title: Instrumental Conducting
courses.description: Study of and experience in instrumental conducting techniques. Problem-solving and decision-making as it pertains to conducting instrumental ensembles to include: transpositions, score study, rehearsal techniques, programming, aural skills, error detection and gesture as effective non-verbal communication.

courses.title: Choral Conducting
courses.description: Study of and experience in choral conducting techniques. Problem-solving and decision-making as it pertains to conducting vocal ensembles. Practical experience in implementing those decisions.

courses.title: Instrumentation and Arranging
courses.description: Study of the instruments of the orchestra and symphonic band. Transpositions, notation, scoring, and arranging for instruments and small ensembles.

courses.title: Brass Fundamentals
courses.description: Fundamentals of playing and teaching the trumpet, trombone, horn, tuba for music majors and minors who plan to teach music in the public schools K-12. Development of embouchure, tone, note reading skills; basic brass pedagogy.

courses.title: Percussion Fundamentals
courses.description: Fundamentals of playing and teaching percussion instruments for music majors and minors who plan to teach music in the public schools K-12; stick and mallet technique for membrane, metal, non-pitched and pitched instruments. Basic percussion pedagogy.

courses.title: String Fundamentals
courses.description: Fundamentals of playing and teaching the violin, viola, cello, and string bass for music majors and minors who plan to teach music in the public schools K-12. Development of bow and finger coordination, tone, note reading skills; basic string pedagogy.

courses.title: Vocal Pedagogy
courses.description: Study of the science and physiology of the vocal instrument and exploration of the teaching of singing based on principles of healthy vocal production. Experience applying acquired knowledge through singing assignments. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 4 units.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 4 units.

courses.title: Woodwind Fundamentals
courses.description: Fundamentals of playing and teaching woodwinds: flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon, and saxophone for music majors and minors who plan to teach music in the public schools K- 12. Development of embouchure, finger coordination, tone, note reading skills; basic woodwind pedagogy.

courses.title: Guitar Fundamentals
courses.description: Fundamentals of playing and teaching guitar for music majors and minors who plan to teach music in the public schools K-12; right- and left-hand techniques for nylon and steel-string guitar pedagogy.

courses.title: Secondary Choral Methods
courses.description: Study and analysis of problems and solutions involved in developing and operating a vocal music program in K-12 schools. Developing the adolescent voice. Common teaching methods, strategies and assessments. 8 hours field observations/service.

courses.title: Secondary Instrumental Methods
courses.description: Study and analysis of problems and solutions involved in developing and operating an instrumental music program in K-12 schools. Common teaching methods, strategies, and assessments. 8 hours field observation/service.
courses.prerequisites: MU 3321A or MU 332; and MU 3341A or MU 334.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken only once Minimum - Maximum Units: 8 hours field observation/service.

courses.title: Teaching Music Literacy
courses.description: Music methods, texts, songs, recordings, and instruments used in the elementary classroom, and their application to literacy building. Investigation of music literacy activities appropriate for various grade levels, including improvisation and composition. Practical strategies for teaching music notation. Application of music to connect across the curriculum.

courses.title: Performance Studio Upper Division
courses.description: Repertoire and technical studies as appropriate for each individual instrument or voice, and at a higher level than MU 1811. Jury examination required. Repeatable up to 5 units. A series of weekly specialized individual instruction lessons for students enrolled in the Music Performance Option only. May be taken up to five times for a total credit of 5 units. A series of weekly specialized individual instruction lessons for students enrolled in the Music Performance Option only. Corequisite(s): MU 2700 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Repeatable up to 5 units.

courses.title: Non-Profit Music
courses.description: Considering Ensembles, orchestras, symphonies, choruses, and opera companies as business operations. Responsibilities of personnel. Financial concerns, grants, and fundraising. Promotion and marketing. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: MU 1040 , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Arranging for Voices
courses.description: Techniques of arranging as well as modifying existing compositions for various vocal ensembles.

courses.title: Jazz Improvisation, Beginning
courses.description: Beginning experience in jazz improvisational techniques. Chords, key, scales, melodic and rhythmic application, stylistic devices and procedures necessary to the development of spontaneous and creative soloistic invention. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.

courses.title: Diction for Singers
courses.description: Study of the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA), pronunciation of languages needed to perform great song and operatic literature. Activities and exercises in Italian, French, German, and English diction. Translating texts into IPA and performance of songs or arias in these languages. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 4 units.
courses.prerequisites: Concurrent enrollment in MU 3811 or MU 4610 , or 2 units from the following: MU 1340 , MU 1770 , or MU 1811 .

courses.title: Interpretation for Singers
courses.description: A performance workshop based on individual student participation in which communication through the singing voice and the special problems of the singer/actor are explored in depth. Improvisation, acting, communication. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 4 units.
courses.prerequisites: MU 1340 or MU 134; 1 unit of MU 177, MU 1770 , MU 1771 or MU 1811 ; Solo performance experience; and non Music majors must audition.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Repeatable up to 4 units.

courses.title: Song Culture for Schools
courses.description: Methods for song leading and strategies for community-building and inclusion of all school constituencies; identifying and developing song resources from around the world. Presentation of singing activities appropriate for various age groups from kindergarten through high school.

courses.title: Guitar Ensemble
courses.description: Study and performance of guitar ensemble literature. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Black Music Ensemble
courses.description: The study, rehearsal, and presentation of classic and contemporary Black American vocal and instrumental repertoire, presented via culturally specific performance practices for the campus and extended community.
courses.prerequisites: Enrollment by audition. Must have prior experience on a relevant instrument.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 9 units, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester.

courses.title: Piano Ensemble
courses.description: Designed to foster collaborative skills in pianists. Sight-reading, rehearsal and performance of piano ensemble repertoire from different eras and styles. Ensembles can include piano four-hands, two-piano, and groups of 3-4 keyboard players on multiple instruments.

courses.title: Jazz Band
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of jazz ensemble and jazz ensemble related music. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Jazz Combo
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of small group jazz and jazz related music.

courses.title: Latin American Ensemble
courses.description: Study and performance of Latin American ensemble literature.

courses.title: Mariachi
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of traditional and contemporary Mariachi repertoire, style, and technique, for the campus and extended communities.
courses.prerequisites: Enrollment by audition. All members must have prior experience on a relevant instrument.

courses.title: Concert Choir
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of choral literature for mixed voices, from all musical periods by composers from around the world. This course is limited to students who have had vocal and/or choral experience in high school or college and who show proficiency for reading and understanding choral literature. This course is limited to students who have had vocal and/or choral experience in high school or college and who show proficiency for reading and understanding choral literature.

courses.title: Chamber Singers
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of choral literature for small choral ensembles, from all musical periods by composers from around the world.
courses.prerequisites: Audition; and required proficiencies determined by audition.

courses.title: Songwriter Showcase
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of song literature and original songwriting.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Piano Ensemble
courses.description: Designed to foster collaborative skills in pianists with performances throughout the semester. Sight-reading, rehearsal and performance of piano ensemble repertoire from different eras and styles. Ensembles can include piano four-hands, two-piano, and groups of 3-10 keyboard players on multiple instruments. Develops ensemble skills such as balance, rhythm and timing when playing with other musicians.
courses.prerequisites: Enrollment by audition. All members must have prior piano playing experience.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 8 units, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester.

courses.title: Collaborative Piano
courses.description: Designed to foster collaborative skills in pianists. Sight-reading, rehearsal and performance of collaborative vocal and instrumental repertoire of many styles. Develops ensemble skills such as balance, rhythm and timing when playing with other musicians. May be taken up to four times for a total credit of 4 units.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 9 units.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Collaborative Piano Ensemble
courses.description: Designed to foster collaborative skills in pianists with performances throughout the semester. Sight-reading, rehearsal and performance of collaborative vocal and instrumental repertoire with piano/pianos, from different eras and styles. Develops ensemble skills such as balance, rhythm and timing when playing with other musicians.
courses.prerequisites: Enrollment by audition. All members must have prior experience on a relevant instrument.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 8 units, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester.

courses.title: Orchestra
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of orchestral literature from all musical periods, styles and genres by composers from around the world. Students from all majors with prior experience on an orchestral instrument may audition and enroll.
courses.prerequisites: Audition and prior training on an orchestral instrument.

courses.title: Wind Ensemble
courses.description: The CPP Wind Ensemble represents the finest woodwind, brass and percussion students at Cal Poly Pomona and exclusively performs wind band literature deemed of the highest quality from the repertory of both traditional and contemporary compositional styles. Comprised of 50 select music majors, minors, and talented non-music majors who qualify through audition, ensemble members will develop a deeper sensitivity toward outstanding musicianship, historical style, performance practices, and aesthetics. In addition, high expectations on individual responsibility to learn his/her part will be required at each rehearsal. An audition and a year-long commitment are required for enrollment. Development of outstanding musicianship, performance practices, and aesthetics.
courses.prerequisites: Enrollment by Audition, prior experience on a wind or percussion instrument, and audition for seat placement.

courses.title: New Music Ensemble
courses.description: Chamber ensemble focusing on repertoire for small and large combinations of instruments with special attention paid towards the workshop and performance of newly composed student and faculty works. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Electronic Music Ensemble
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of MIDI and electronic works of a variety of genres from around the world. May be taken unlimited times.
courses.prerequisites: Audition; and prior training a related band string, keyboard or voice instrument.

courses.title: String Ensemble
courses.description: Study, rehearsal and performance of string orchestra and chamber ensemble literature from all musical periods by composers from around the world.
courses.prerequisites: Audition; and Minimum 2 years of instrument experience.

courses.title: Music Theatre Workshop
courses.description: Rehearsal and preparation for performance of operatic, operetta, and musical theatre literature. Students enrolled in MU 3621L are required to enroll in MU 3631L for semesters in which one production is in rehearsal/performance over a two-semester period. MU 3631L and MU 3621L are a sequence requiring a one year commitment from the student.

courses.title: Music Theatre Production
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of a complete opera, operetta, or musical theatre or performance of selections from these genres. Technical crews, singing, and acting. Students enrolled in MU 3631L are required to enroll in MU 3621L for semesters in which one production is in rehearsal/performance over a two-semester period. MU 3621L and MU 3631L are a sequence requiring a one year commitment from the student.
courses.prerequisites: Audition, and singing and acting proficiency.

courses.title: African American Vocal Ensemble
courses.description: Rehearsal and performance of jazz and jazz related vocal ensemble music.

courses.title: World Music Ensemble
courses.description: Study and performance of Soul ensemble literature.

courses.title: Percussion Ensemble
courses.description: Study and performance of chamber to large percussion ensemble literature.

courses.title: Symphonic Winds
courses.description: This ensemble performs repertory of both traditional and contemporary compositional styles. Comprised of 50-60 select music majors, minors and talented non-music majors who qualify through audition, ensemble members will develop a deeper sensitivity toward outstanding musicianship, historical style, performance practices, and aesthetics. In addition, high expectations on individual responsibility to learn his/her part will be required at each rehearsal. An audition and a year-long commitment are required for enrollment.
courses.prerequisites: Enrollment by Audition, prior experience on a wind or percussion instrument, and audition for seat placement.

courses.title: Woodwind Ensemble
courses.description: Study and performance of chamber to large woodwind ensemble literature. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Brass Ensemble
courses.description: Study and performance of chamber to large brass ensemble literature.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Undergraduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
